To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the light trigger for rhabdom breakdown at dawn in the lateral eye of Limulud polyphemus may be transduced via a Ca(2+), diacylglycerols and protein kinase C signal transduction pathway, and that this pathway may be mediated by PKC beta II.

(1) PKC is a likely candidate for mediating the light trigger for rhabdom renewal in the Limulus lateral eye, (2) DAG is a likely candidate as an endogenous PKC activator in the Limulus rhabdom, and (3) PKC beta II and zeta are the most likely candidates as the PKC isozymes involved in the light triggering and renewal of rhabdoms in the Limulus compound lateral eye.

PKC is required for rhabdom sheddding in Limulus photoreceptors, that DAG analogs can elicit rhabdome shedding in the absence of light, and that DAG analogs and InsP3 synergize to elicit rhamdome shedding at low concentrations of the former.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding the molecular mechanisms whereby a signal transduction cascade is triggered by the light trigger and by circadian eferent input to the Limulus eye, which in turn initiates the daily breakdown of photosensitive membrane.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms whereby light triggers the daily breakdown and renewal of the photoreceptor membrane in the horseshoe-crab eye.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms whereby the trigger light is converted into a signal that initiates the breakdown and renewal of the photosensitive membranes of photoreceptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the retinal wrecking crews of Limulus and vertebrates are not only very similar in their function but also in the molecular mechanisms by which the light trigger is transduced.
the light trigger is transduced to the intracellular signaling machinery via a DAG-PKC pathway, and that this pathway is likely to be the same in both Limulus and vertebrate photoreceptor cells.
light triggers the rhabdom shedding process via a Ca(2+), diacylglyceride (DAG), and protein kinase C (PKG) cascade.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
light triggers rhibdom shedding via a Ca(2+)--DAG--PKC signaling pathway.
the light trigger for rhabdom renewal in Limulus is mediated through the activation of a PKC isozyme, and this is achieved via the production of InsP3 and DAG.
the light trigger for rhabdom renewal in Limulus is communicated by the activation of PKC via the DAG/InsP3/Ca(2+) pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the light trigger for rhabdom renewal is mediated by a Ca(2+)--PKC signaling cascade.
the retinal wrecking team is composed of a signal transduction cascade involving the light trigger, DAG, InsP3, and PKC.
the retinal wrecking crews of vertebrates and invertebrates have a common mechanism of activation.
